terms.definition: A mathematical machine with states and transitions.
terms.usage: Use the singular form for one machine; use automata/autômatos for the plural.

terms.definition: A node representing one configuration of an automaton.
A rule that moves a machine between states.
terms.usage: Use consistently in editors, simulations, and errors.

terms.definition: A formal system of variables, terminals, and productions.
terms.usage: Reserve rule for an individual production rule.

terms.definition: Determine how an input is derived by a grammar.
terms.usage: The established Parser tool name may remain Parser; explanatory copy uses análise sintática.

terms.definition: The readable and writable storage used by a Turing machine.
terms.usage: Use fita for both single-tape and multi-tape machines.

terms.definition: Last-in, first-out storage used by a pushdown automaton.
terms.usage: Do not use the untranslated English term in Portuguese interface copy.

terms.definition: Symbols or values produced by a computation.
terms.usage: Use for both a transducer result and a produced token sequence.

terms.definition: Conclude that an input belongs to the recognized language.
terms.usage: Use accepted/aceita for the completed outcome; do not substitute halt.

terms.definition: Conclude that an input does not belong to the recognized language.
terms.usage: Use rejected/rejeitada for the completed outcome; do not use for an unknown bounded result.

terms.definition: Stop executing because no further computation step is taken.
terms.usage: Halting alone does not imply acceptance or rejection unless the machine policy says so.

terms.definition: A bounded computation outcome that cannot establish acceptance or rejection.
terms.usage: Do not translate as rejected; explain the reached limit when space allows.

terms.definition: The unique string containing no symbols, commonly written ε.
terms.usage: Keep ε as notation; localize its explanatory label.

terms.definition: A necessary property used to reason about classes of formal languages.
terms.usage: Use title capitalization according to locale: Pumping Lemma in English headings and Lema do bombeamento in Portuguese headings; use lowercase in running prose unless sentence-initial.

terms.definition: The application area dedicated to one formal-system family.
terms.usage: Use the translated term in prose and accessibility labels.
